clue.text: Scared? That's awful!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation that something is dreadful or terrible

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the word's everyday meaning of afraid; the second is the older sense of something inspiring dread, as in a fearful mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both frightened and, of a thing, dreadful or terrible, so it covers a scared person and an awful situation.

clue.text: Strain's made the salesman turn firm recently

indicators.note: turn tells us the word for a salesman is flipped round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
late can mean recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: A firm's sales rep has been under strain since the business changed hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' flips the salesman word round. 'Strain' looks like a noun of stress, but the verb sense is filtering; the 's made the' is joining material.
explanation.definitionFit: To percolate is to filter a liquid slowly through something, which is straining it.

clue.text: A flighty creature's usual nonsense

parts.note: par is the usual or normal level, as in 'par for the course'
rot is a common word for nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone flighty talks the usual nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' suggests a giddy person, but here it just means able to fly: the definition is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird is a creature of flight, and this talking species is a familiar example.

clue.text: A don can change — and a crawler

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the three words before it

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A university don can alter his ways and still be a sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges A DON CAN into ANACOND, then the final 'a' is added. 'crawler' suggests a toady, but here it is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: This huge South American snake moves along the ground, so it is a crawler in the literal sense.

clue.text: Preparation of main French feast representing liberation

indicators.note: preparation means working ingredients into a new form, so the letters of the next three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand French banquet is prepared to celebrate the freeing of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preparation of' rearranges the fifteen letters of MAIN FRENCH FEAST; 'representing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfranchisement in its old sense is the freeing of a slave or serf, which is liberation.

clue.text: At fifty caper in the sea

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an antic is a playful caper or prank

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old larks about while swimming in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caper' looks like a verb about someone at fifty, but it is a noun giving ANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean between Europe and the Americas is often loosely called a sea.

clue.text: A little Scot, terribly bad-tempered little beast

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Scot who is a little terribly bad-tempered is called a nasty little beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' points to a short run inside SCOT TERRIBLY, crossing the gap between the words.
explanation.definitionFit: This small river mammal is a little beast, and one can be fierce when cornered.

clue.text: Fed-up — at the last minute let down

indicators.note: in a down clue up tells us the word before is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
late means at the last minute, almost too late

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with plans that were cancelled at the last minute feels let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed-up' reads as one word meaning annoyed, but 'up' in this down clue turns the first three letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To let down a tyre or balloon is to release its air, which is the literal sense of the verb.

clue.text: Exercise hard. Note little cash is required

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
set means hardened, as concrete or jelly sets
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Exercise is hard work, and you need hardly any money for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition calls it 'little' because the old Spanish coin was worth very little.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the former unit of Spanish money, a coin of small value replaced by the euro.

clue.text: Stick by the river, being a stout fellow

indicators.note: by means beside, so the stick is placed next to the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a staff is a walking stick or pole

explanation.surface: A sturdy man stands with his walking stick beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The FAL is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England. 'stout fellow' sounds like praise for a good chap, but it means a fat man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John, Shakespeare's fat knight in the Henry IV plays, is literature's best-known stout man.

clue.text: He'll get a professional medico

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: one who gets or obtains things

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a medico, a doctor, is one who cures

explanation.surface: A man says he'll find a proper qualified doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He'll get' looks like the start of a sentence but defines a person who obtains.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurer is one who obtains or acquires something for others.

clue.text: Typical of a woman trainee

parts.note: Norma is a woman's name
L, from the L-plate, stands for a learner driver

explanation.surface: Typical of a woman who is still in training.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner sign that new British drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usual or standard is what you would expect, the ordinary state of things.

clue.text: Taking a slug in a flash

parts.note: a slug is slang for a bullet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a slug of drink in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slug' suggests a gulp of whisky and 'in a flash' a moment; in fact a slug is a bullet, and a flash is a news item.
explanation.definitionFit: A news flash is a short urgent announcement of news.

clue.text: Feature about heartless lad concerned with 22

definitions.note: the solution to 22 down, read in its legal sense of offspring

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a feature goes round the rest

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of lad is taken away

parts.note: re means concerning, as at the head of a letter

explanation.surface: A face is described as being all about a lad with no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle of the boy; 'about' wraps the face feature round him and the 'concerned with' word. The definition is a cross-reference to another entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry 22 in its legal sense means descendants or offspring, as in dying without heirs.

clue.text: Denouncing the mother country

definitions.note: a verb form used as a noun, the act of condemning

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, a horse for instance
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone is criticising their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Dam for mother is used of livestock, especially horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation, a fierce cursing of someone or something.

clue.text: Making a move about the old king's wood

indicators.note: about means round, so a shove is wrapped around the king

parts.note: a shove is a pushing move
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Moving against the old king, rebels take to the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgius Rex is the Latin monogram of King George. 'about' wraps the push round him; 'Making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove of ash trees is a small wood.

clue.text: Social gathering for those who have come down

definitions.text: Social gathering for those who have come down

parts.words: Social gathering for those who have come down
parts.note: the people who have come down are skiers back from the slopes, and this is their evening socialising

explanation.walkthrough: 'come down' suggests leaving university or a drug high; it means skiing down the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for after skiing, the drinks and parties at a resort when the day's runs are done.

clue.text: Slick winger, a model

parts.note: pat means glib or slick, as in a pat answer
a tern is a seabird, a creature with wings

explanation.surface: A smooth wing forward on the football team is held up as a role model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' looks like a footballer but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a template or example to copy, which is what a model is.

clue.text: Churchman backing up mere slapdash painter

indicators.note: in a down clue backing up means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman

indicators.note: slapdash means carelessly done, so the letters of mere are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clergyman supports a merely careless artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' turns REV into VER; 'slapdash' turns MERE into MEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the Dutch master who painted Girl with a Pearl Earring.

clue.text: The dog's a bounder!

definitions.meaning: a breed of spaniel used for flushing game
one who bounds or leaps, rather than the old word for a cad

explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' suggests a cad, but here it is literal: one who leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: This spaniel breed is named for springing game from cover, and anything that leaps is a jumper.

clue.text: Trained revolutionary carrying a listening device

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the revolutionary encloses the listening device

parts.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary
the ear is what we listen with

explanation.surface: A trained revolutionary is fitted with a bugging device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening device' suggests a bug, but it is just the human ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear animals or children is to bring them up, training and raising them.

clue.text: Suspend the procession

definitions.meaning: hang up, as in to ... up a line of lights
a line of people or things one after another

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspend' and 'the procession' look like a single instruction; they are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something by a cord is one sense, and a sequence of horses or people following each other is another.

clue.text: Put out — is to go to court

parts.note: taken as written
to sue is to take legal action in court

explanation.surface: Someone who is annoyed is going to take legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as annoyed, but it means to publish or release.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to publish or release something, such as a statement or stamps.

clue.text: The average hour allowed as an interval

parts.note: the mean is the arithmetic average
an hour is a time, as in 'the hour has come'

explanation.surface: An average hour is set aside for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The average hour' calls up Greenwich Mean Time, and 'allowed as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The period between two events is the interval in between, the time while waiting.

clue.text: Men get so excited finding something of great value

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men become thrilled on discovering a priceless treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges MEN GET SO; 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone such as a diamond or ruby is a jewel prized for its worth.

clue.text: The Spanish work the editor ran off

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
op, short for opus, is a work
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A Spanish editor runs away from his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran off' looks like printing copies, but it means fled to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, typically to get married.

clue.text: In this locality conservationists appear essential

parts.note: taken as written
here means this place
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Conservationists in this area seem to be indispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrinsic is part of a thing's basic nature, permanently built in.
